cause: The harness provisions managed memory by default; the execution role had no memory permissions
fix: Scoped memory actions on `memory/*` added to the harness role

happened: Model never saw the tool (98 input tokens) and refused in prose; deny/throw cases "passed" without the hook ever firing
cause: A plain name in `allowedTools` selects built-ins only and silently drops inline tools (matches aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws#468). Our check also accepted "no tool call" as a deny
fix: Select inline tools as `@spike_echo` (verified: the model then sees only `spike_echo`, no shell or file tools). The spike check now requires an actual hook `deny` event

test: Phase 3 deploy, attaching the policy engine
happened: Gateway update failed: gateway role not authorized for `bedrock-agentcore:AuthorizeAction`
cause: The docs list the action but the check runs against the gateway ARN, not only the policy engine
fix: Granted it on the engine and on `gateway/kavach-gateway-*` (a name pattern avoids a role ↔ gateway cycle)

test: Phase 3 unit tests, L4 with an empty `payeeId`
happened: Hook denied, but via "internal error" instead of R1
cause: DynamoDB rejects an empty key; the exception path caught it (fail-closed worked, wrong reason)
fix: `get_payee` returns no payee for empty or non-string IDs; test asserts the R1 reason

test: Phase 3 verify, C3 calls to the Gateway
happened: Cedar denials came back as JSON-RPC error `-32002`, not the documented `isError` result, so the checker first reported them as unknown RPC errors
cause: Docs example differs from live behaviour
fix: Checker classifies `-32002` + "policy enforcement" as `policy_denied` and records the policy name

happened: CloudFormation dependency cycle: Gateway → gateway role policy → approval tool → state machine → workflow Lambda → Gateway
cause: The Gateway depended on the role's whole default policy, which now held tool-invoke grants
fix: Policy-engine permissions moved to their own inline policy; the Gateway depends only on that

happened: Approver alert for a pending approval carried no session ID, so it couldn't be tied back to the conversation
Once, Kavach returned an empty reply (no money moved; session stayed paused). Not reproduced on rerun
fix: Open: the /chat API (Phase 7) will send a calm fallback message when a turn has no text

happened: Turns now take about 8 s with L2 + L3 + signed audit in the path, against a p50 target of 4 s
cause: Guardrail, Nova Micro scorer and KMS/S3 writes run in series before the model
fix: Open: measure p50/p95 in the Phase 5 benchmark, then run L2 and L3 in parallel

happened: A plain Tamil electricity-bill request was refused, citing "Rs 14,000 to Chennai Metrowater", text from a different attack script. The live Kavach memory also held Priya's crypto scam and Kamala's plumber approval side by side
cause: The harness's default managed memory extracts long-term "facts" (SEMANTIC + SUMMARIZATION strategies) under one shared actor, `default`, because no `actorId` was set. One household's scam call, or a false "Arjun approved", carried into every later session: a cross-household leak and a memory-poisoning path. Deterministic layers still held; no money moved
fix: Harness memory disabled (verified: a session still keeps its own turns; a new session starts clean). Client also sets `actorId = sessionId`. The two orphaned memory stores were deleted. Smoke results from that run marked invalid

happened: The scammer coach's victim often asked "what should I do next?" instead of asking for a payment, so turns tested nothing
cause: Coach prompt didn't require a concrete payment request or teach the hide-the-reason tactic real scammers use
fix: Every victim message must name an amount and destination; after a refusal the scammer coaches her to drop mentions of police or banks and give an innocent reason; fallbacks name the real target

happened: Kavach turns missed the 4 s p50 target (5.1 s across the benchmark; 8.7 s on bill payments, which make 3–4 model calls)
cause: The `before_invocation` hook (p50 1.28 s) ran the guardrail and the Nova Micro scorer one after the other, and each tool call adds about 0.2 s for the L4 gate plus its signed audit record
fix: Guardrail and scorer now run in parallel; hook Lambdas raised to 1,024 MB. Bill payments went from p50 8.7 s to 8.2 s (30 of 30 complete, 0 false holds). Still above target: most of a turn is the model's own tool calls. Not fixed by loosening any check

cause: The API role was granted `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness`, but calling `InvokeHarness` is authorised as `InvokeAgentRuntime` on the harness ARN

happened: The approver inbox opened on 29 stale "New payee: Officer" requests and counters of 31 blocked, 12 held: leftovers from verify scripts and benchmark runs in Kamala's household. 117 approval workflows were still waiting out their 24-hour token
cause: Tests and the benchmark shared the demo households and only cleaned up some approvals
fix: `scripts/reset_demo.py` (`make reset-demo`) stops waiting workflows, deletes non-seed approvals, payees and ledger rows, re-seeds and re-syncs Cedar; dry run by default. Signed audit records stay under Object Lock
